newsitem.title: USA: Floods to halt Minneapolis-area grain operations.
newsitem.headline: Floods to halt Minneapolis-area grain operations.

text.p: Rising river water and flooded rail lines will halt operations at some grain elevators in the Minneapolis-suburb of Savage this week, grain company officials said.
"We will be stopping inbound truck traffic the next couple of days," said a Continental Grain Co official regarding the company's Savage terminal near the Minnesota River.
Rising water on the Minnesota River will make it necessary to close a gate in the levee surrounding Continental's elevator, which will halt traffic to it, said the Continental official.

The St. Paul Army Corps of Engineers office said the Minnesota River was forecast to crest April 14 at 716 feet above sea level at Savage, 18 feet above flood stage. As of late Sunday the river was at 708.5 feet above sea level.

Harvest States Cooperatives will suspend rail shipments at its Savage facility once two grain cars are loaded and shipped. Truck shipments should be suspended in two days, said Tim Paurus, Harvest States' director of terminal operations.
"We have some cars in today we will load out and they will be the last," he said.
The barge dock at Cargill Inc's Savage elevator is underwater, but no water has reached the main terminal, said Cargill spokeswoman Lori Johnson.
"We are not anticipating water in the facility," she said.
The three elevators have not loaded any grain barges this season because of high water on the river and the lack of empty barges coming north. Spring barge loadings normally begin in late March.
Flood waters have not reached the Continental terminal, nor the Harvest States facility, where, according to Paurus, a berm may be built around a low-lying loading area.

Railroads said Monday they suspended service on some lines in southern Minnesota because of flooding. Harvest States' Paurus said the railroads should allow rail cars to leave the area but will not allow anymore in.
